rows.speaker: جماعة من السلف
rows.claim: A group of early authorities treated al-Anfal and Bara'a as one surah, which they saw as explaining their arrangement.
rows.anchor: قال جماعة من السلف : أنهما سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rationale for placing Bara'a here is its length: among the six preceding surahs, none is longer, which is enough to establish affinity.
rows.anchor: وضع براءة هنا لمناسبة الطول فإنه ليس بعد الست السابقة سورة أطول منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third rationale says placing the pair amid the seven long surahs, whose order was known early, signals that their placement was not fixed by revelation and that the Prophet died before explaining them.
rows.anchor: خلل بالسورتين أثناء السبع الطول المعلوم ترتيبها في العصر الأول للإشارة إلى أن ذلك أمر صادر لا عن توقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi calls the non-tawqifi explanation very far-fetched, citing his earlier discussion; the question to the Jewish scholar and Uthman's answer do not explicitly establish it.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره من عدم التوقيف في هذا الوضع في غاية البعد كما يفهم مما قدمناه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A fourth arrangement proposal would move Yunus ahead and place Hud after Bara'a, as in Ubayy's codex, to preserve the seven-long sequence.
rows.anchor: لو أخرهما وقدم يونس وأتى بعد براءة بهود كما في مصحف أبي لمراعاة مناسبة السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus has a stronger connection with the next five surahs through shared stories, alif-lam-ra openings, mention of the Book, Meccan origin, comparable length apart from al-Hijr, and names of prophets; al-Ra'd is a fitting angelic name alongside them.
rows.anchor: الأولى بسورة يونس أن يؤتى بالسور الخمس التي بعدها لما اشتركت فيه من المناسبات من القصص والإفتتاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These multiple links between Yunus and the following surahs outweigh the single consideration for placing Yunus immediately after al-A'raf.
rows.anchor: وهي آكد من هذا الوجه الواحد في تقديم يونس بعد الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same links partly explain placing al-Hijr before al-Nahl despite its shorter length; moving Bara'a after six shorter surahs would make the connection much weaker because Bara'a is exceptionally long.
rows.anchor: ولو أخرت براءة عن هذه السور الست لبعدت المناسبة جدا لطولها بعد عدة سور أقصر منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah openings help explain placing al-Hijr before al-Nahl and Aal Imran before al-Nisa, but this opening-based rationale is not consistent throughout the Quran's arrangement.
rows.anchor: يشهد لمراعاة الفواتح في مناسبة الوضع ما ذكرناه من تقديم الحجر على النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud's codex placed the seven long surahs in descending length, then the hundred-verse surahs similarly, with Anfal after al-Nur.
rows.anchor: أن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قدم في مصحفه البقرة والنساء وآل عمران والأعراف والأنعام والمائدة ويونس راعى السبع الطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement of Anfal after al-Nur links al-Nur's promise that believers will inherit the land with Anfal's reminder of their earlier weakness, presenting the promised outcome as fulfilled.
rows.anchor: فإن الأولى مشتملة على الوعد بما حصل وذكر به في الثانية

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas reports from Uthman that Anfal and Bara'a were called the twin surahs in the Prophet's time, so he placed them among the seven long surahs.
rows.anchor: أخرج النحاس في ناسخه عنه أنه قال : كانت الأنفال وبراءة يدعيان في زمن رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The identity of the seventh long surah is disputed: Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, and one Ibn Abbas report say Yunus; another report from Ibn Abbas in al-Hakim says al-Kahf; other scholars end the set with Bara'a, while another view counts Anfal and Bara'a together.
rows.anchor: ليس أمرا مجمعا عليه بل هو قول مجاهد وابن جبير ورواية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the question to the Jewish scholar and Uthman's reply are not explicit evidence that the surah placement was not divinely fixed.
rows.anchor: وسؤال الحبر وجواب عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنهما ليسا نصا في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the earlier scholar's first proposed rationale conflicts with the apparent question, which suggests omission of the basmala from Bara'a was itself a matter of judgment.
rows.anchor: في أول الأمور التي فتح الله تعالى بها عليه غير ملائم بظاهره ظاهر سؤال الحبر رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says God granted him an explanation of this surah's connection to the preceding one that the earlier eminent scholar had not supplied.
rows.anchor: قد من الله تعالى على هذا العبد الحقير بما لم يمن به على هذا الجليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers addressed are the familiar group of Abu Sufyan and his companions.
rows.anchor: أي المعهودين وهم أبو سفيان وأصحابه

rows.speaker: جمع
rows.claim: A group takes the lām as causal: the Prophet is told to say this for the disbelievers' benefit.
rows.anchor: واللام عند جمع للتعليل أي قل لأجلهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the lām as transmission: the Prophet must convey the meaning contained in the quoted sentence, whether or not he uses its exact wording.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الظاهر أن اللام للتبليغ وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أمر أن يقول هذا المعنى

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop opposing the Messenger by entering Islam, their previous sins are forgiven, including hostility and spending to support misguidance.
rows.anchor: عما هم فيه من معاداة الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads the clause in the second person, 'if you desist, you will be forgiven'; on this reading the lām is necessarily for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: وأما على قراءة ابن مسعود ( إن تنتهوا يغفر لكم ( بالخطاب فلا خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading, 'it will be forgiven for them,' makes the pronoun refer to God.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( بغفر لهم ) على أن الضمير لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent is God's recurring treatment of those who conspire against prophets: He supports believers against them, defeats them, and destroys them.
rows.anchor: عادة الله تعالى الجارية في الذين تحزبوا على الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام من نصر المؤمنين عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent is attributed to earlier peoples by association, as in 'a precedent of those We sent' though it is God's precedent carried out through the messengers; al-Alusi cites 17:77 as the parallel.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك قوله سبحانه : ( سنة من قد أرسلنا ) فأضاف السنة إلى المرسلين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the earlier peoples specifically with those whose plotting rebounded on them at Badr; al-Alusi prefers the general interpretation because a sunnah conventionally recurs, even though a habit may be established once.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم فسره بذلك ولعل الأول أولى لعمومه ولأن السنة تقتضي التكرر في العرف

words: وَإِن يَعُودُوا۟ فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause supplies the consequence elliptically: if they return, God will exact vengeance or give the believers victory, as al-Bahr explains.
rows.anchor: والجملة على ما في البحر دليل الجواب والتقدير إن يعودوا انتقمنا منهم أو نصرنا المؤمنين عليهم

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Others read the disbelievers generally: abandoning disbelief and becoming Muslim erases prior disbelief and sins, while apostasy back to disbelief restores God's domination over them.
rows.anchor: وذهب غير واحد إلى أن المراد بالذين كفروا الكفار مطلقا والآية حث على الإيمان وترغيب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is cited for Islam erasing what preceded it, so a convert need not make up missed prayer, zakat, or fasting, or compensate for property or life lost before conversion.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على أن الإسلام يجب ما قبله وأن الكافر إذا أسلم لا يخاطب بقضاء ما فاته من صلاة

rows.speaker: المالكية
rows.claim: The Malikis extend this rule to a repentant apostate and cite the verse to cancel pre-Islamic jizya owed by a dhimmi who converts.
rows.anchor: وأجرى المالكية ذلك كله في المرتد إذا تاب لعموم الآية

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits through Ibn Wahb that Malik said a disbeliever who converts is not held accountable for anything done during disbelief, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق ابن وهب عن مالك قال : لا يؤاخذ الكافر بشيء صنعه في كفره إذا أسلم

rows.speaker: بعض
rows.claim: One view says a converted combatant disbeliever has no outstanding liability, while a protected non-Muslim owes no divine duties but remains liable for human claims.
rows.anchor: قال بعض : إن الحربي إذا أسلم لم تبق عليه تبعة أصلا وأما الذمي فلا يلزمه قضاء حقوق الله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa is reported to treat a repentant apostate like the Malikis, clearing prior liabilities; some even attribute to him that lifelong sin followed by apostasy and return leaves no sin, an attribution al-Alusi calls highly strange.
rows.anchor: ونسب إلى الإمام أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه أن مذهبه في المرتد كمذهب المالكية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: A report in Ibn Abd al-Haqq's Quran-law work says Abu Hanifa and Malik preserve human claims against the apostate but clear claims belonging to God; al-Shafi'i requires all claims to be discharged.
rows.anchor: كما في كتاب أحكام القرآن لابن عبد الحق وخالفهما الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه وقال : يلزمه جميع الحقوق

rows.speaker: شمس الأئمة الحلواني
rows.claim: Al-Halwani says an apostate returning to Islam must make up prayers and fasts he deliberately missed while Muslim; the apostasy does not erase those deliberate omissions.
rows.anchor: قال شمس الأئمة الحلواني : عليه قضاء ما ترك الصلاة والصيام معصية تبقى بعد الردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi cites al-Khaniyya's detailed rulings to show that the formula 'human rights remain, divine rights lapse' is not absolute for apostates.
rows.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن قولهم المرتد يلزمه حقوق العباد دون حقوق الله تعالى ليس على إطلاقه

rows.speaker: قاضيخان
rows.claim: Al-Khaniyya distinguishes where property, retaliation, or defamation claims arose: after apostasy in enemy territory and flight, they are waived on return, but claims arising before that remain enforceable.
rows.anchor: مسلم أصاب مالا أو شيئا يجب به القصاص أو حد قذف ثم ارتد أو أصاب ذلك وهو مرتد في دار الإسلام

rows.speaker: قاضيخان
rows.claim: For divine limits committed before or after apostasy and flight, Al-Khaniyya generally waives punishment on return, except stolen property and specified homicide or road-banditry compensation, whose liability depends on when the act occurred.
rows.anchor: فكل ذلك يكون موضوعا عنه إلا أنه يضمن المال في السرقة وإذا أصاب دما في الطريق كان عليه القصاص

rows.speaker: قاضيخان
rows.claim: For drinking, apostasy before conversion prevents a new limit from being imposed; if the offense occurs while imprisoned, wine penalties are treated differently from other divine limits and depend on whether the ruler already has custody.
rows.anchor: وإن وجب على المسلم حد الشرب ثم ارتد ثم أسلم قبل اللحوق بدار الحرب فإنه لا يؤاخذ بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the context best fits original disbelief: 'what preceded' means what was done while originally disbelieving, and Islam erases that, as in the report from Amr ibn al-As in Muslim that Islam, emigration, and pilgrimage erase what came before.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الوجه في الآية هو المطابق لمقتضى المقام وأن المتبادر من الكفر الكفر الأصلي

rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: In a report in Muslim, Amr ibn al-As asks the Prophet to stipulate forgiveness at his pledge; the Prophet replies that Islam erases what came before, as do emigration and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أخرجه مسلم عن عمرو بن العاص قال : أتيت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi cautions that 'what' in the hadith cannot mean absolutely everything in each of its three clauses.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ( ما ) لا يمكن حملها في الكل على العموم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say a convert must also repent and regret past acts, alongside faith, in order to be forgiven; al-Alusi expresses reservation about this qualification.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الكافر إذا أسلم يلزمه التوبة والندم على ما سلف مع الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite men and women resemble one another in hypocrisy as parts of one thing, sharing the same nature and outward form; this gathers up their previously described faults.
rows.anchor: أي متشابهون في النفاق كتشابه أبعاض الشيء الواحد والمراد الاتحاد في الحقيقة والصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may connect with the hypocrites' oath that they are among the believers and refute it by affirming 'they are not of you'; alternatively it summarizes all their faults. In either construction, min expresses connection, as in the hadith 'You are to me as Aaron was to Moses.'
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي متصلة بقوله تعالى : ( يحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم ) والمراد منها تكذيب قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly mentioning the women signals how deeply rooted the group is in disbelief and hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لأحوال الإناث للإيذان بكمال عراقتهم في الكفر والنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their commanding wrong means urging denial of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي بالتكذيب بالنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as reported by Ibn Abi Hatim, identifies the good they suppress as the testimony that there is no god but God and acknowledgment of what God revealed.
rows.anchor: كما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says every instance of munkar in the Quran means worship of idols and Satan; al-Alusi allows the terms here to include those examples and other wrongs and goods.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن أبي العالية أنه قال : كل منكر ذكر في القرآن المراد منه عبادة الأوثان والشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may stand independently to reinforce what came before and reveal how they oppose believers, or serve as a second predicate.
rows.anchor: والجملة استئناف مقرر لمضمون ما سبق مفصح عن مضادة حالهم لحال المؤمنين أو خبر ثان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan explain the phrase as withholding expenditure in obedience to God; clasping the hand is a metaphor for stinginess, just as extending it signifies generosity.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن وقبض اليد كناية عن الشح والبخل كما أن بسطها كناية عن الجود

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the phrase means holding back from jihad, but al-Alusi rejects this as contrary to the common usage of the expression.
rows.anchor: وعن الجبائي أن المراد يمسكون أيديهم عن الجهاد في سبيل الله تعالى وهو خلاف الشائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God is metaphorical for abandoning obedience to Him.
rows.anchor: النسيان مجاز عن الترك وهو كناية عن ترك الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgetting them means withholding His grace and favor; the wording echoes their own forgetting by way of verbal correspondence.
rows.anchor: منع لطفه وفضله عنهم والتعبير بالنسيان للمشاكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the most complete in rebellion and departure from obedience, rhetorically described as though they were the whole category; the restriction is justified by the separating pronoun and definite predicate despite other sinners.
rows.anchor: الكاملون في التمرد والفسق الذي هو الخروج عن الطاعة والانسلاخ عن كل حتى كأنهم الجنس كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage describes believers' good state now and in the hereafter after describing their opponents' state in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: بيان لحسن حال المؤمنين والمؤمنات حالا ومآلا بعد بيان حال أضدادهم عاجلا وآجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mutual guardianship contrasts with the earlier description of hypocrites as one another's kind; the wording changes to convey mutual support and solidarity.
rows.anchor: يقابل قوله تعالى فيما مر : ( بعضهم من بعض ) وتغيير الأسلوب للإشارة إلى تناصرهم وتعاضدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining good and forbidding wrong explicitly reverses the hypocrites' behavior; the discussion of good and wrong is the same as above.
rows.anchor: ظاهر المقابلة ( ليأمرون بالمنكر ) الخ الكلام في المنكر والمعروف معروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer contrasts with the hypocrites' forgetting God, and adds special praise of believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو في مقابلة ( نسوا الله ) وقوله سبحانه : ( ويقيمون الصلاة ) زيادة مدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paying zakat reverses the hypocrites' grasping their hands shut.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة ( يقبضون أيديهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They obey God and His Messenger in all matters, in contrast to the hypocrites' complete rebellion; another view makes this specifically contrast their forgetting God.
rows.anchor: أي في سائر الأمور في مقابلة وصف المنافقين بكمال الفسق والخروج عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promised mercy contrasts with His withholding grace from hypocrites; another interpretation contrasts it with their being called rebellious, since the righteous are the pious and recipients of mercy.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة ( فنسيهم ) المفسر بمنع لطفه ورحمته سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the believers and women believers characterized by the preceding excellent qualities; its distant form carries the emphasis discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى المؤمنين والمؤمنات باعتبار اتصافهم بما سلف من الصفات الجليلة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and others say the future particle strengthens the promise of mercy.
rows.anchor: على ما قال الزمخشري وتبعه غير واحد لتأكيد الوعد

rows.speaker: صاحب التقريب
rows.claim: The author of al-Taqrib argues that the future particle emphasizes whatever follows because affirmation with sa- contrasts with negation by lan, whether the result is promise, threat, or something else.
rows.anchor: ووجه ذلك بأن السين في الإثبات في مقابلة لن في النفي فتكون بهذا الاعتبار تأكيدا لما دخلت عليه

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar rejects the claim that sa- itself guarantees the promised outcome: certainty comes from context, and he says the claim serves al-Zamakhshari's mistaken doctrine that reward is necessary.
rows.anchor: وقال العلامة ابن حجر : ما زعمه الزمخشري من أن السين تفيد القطع بمدخولها مردود

rows.speaker: ابن قاسم
rows.claim: Ibn Qasim counters Ibn Hajar's criticism: a transmitted point cannot be dismissed by that argument, and accusing the imams of inattention arises from a desire to object.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه الفهامة ابن قاسم بأن هذا لا وجه له لأنه أمر نقلي لا يدفعه ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty, able to do anything and never prevented from willing it, and wise, placing things where they belong, including reward and punishment; this grounds the promised mercy.
rows.anchor: يضع الأشياء مواضعها ومن ذلك النعمة والنقمة والجملة تعليل للوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God gave them from His bounty, they withheld the right due to God from it.
rows.anchor: أي منعوا حق الله تعالى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned away from obedience to God.
rows.anchor: أي أعرضوا عن طاعة الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may be independent or circumstantial; their established habit of turning from obedience explains their conduct, and that continuing habit does not conflict with either syntax.
rows.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة أو حالية والاستمرار المقتضى للتقدم لا ينافي ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation distinguishes an outward turning away in their bodies from inward aversion in their hearts.
rows.anchor: والمراد على ما قيل : تولوا بأجرامهم وهم معرضون بقلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of 'Did they not know?' may be the hypocrites or those who made a covenant with God.
rows.anchor: أي المنافقون أو من عاهد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali is reported to have read the verb with second-person ta, addressing the believers; another view takes it as an address to the first group by a shift in person.
rows.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قرأ بالتاء على أنه خطاب للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the address as a second shift in person is strained because the following phrase says God knows their secret and private talk.
rows.anchor: على الالتفات ويأباه قوله تعالى : أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to hypocrites, their secret is concealed hypocrisy and their private talk is mutual slander; if they refer to covenant-makers, the secret is intent to break the pledge and the talk is calling zakat a tax.
rows.anchor: ما أسروه في أنفسهم من النفاق ومن النجوى ما يتناجون به من المطاعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret is mentioned before private conversation because, in ordinary perception, knowing what is secret is more awe-inspiring; the ordering can hasten awe or reassurance according to the readings.
rows.anchor: وتقديم السر على النجوى لأن العلم به أعظم في الشاهد من العلم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative either rebukes and threatens them for daring such grave acts despite knowing God's awareness, or prompts acknowledgment that He will punish and requite them; naming God explicitly cultivates awe and magnifies the reckoning.
rows.anchor: والهمزة إما للإنكار والتوبيخ والتهديد أي ألم يعلموا ذلك حتى اجترأوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being the all-knower of unseen things means nothing at all is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: فلا يخفى عليه سبحانه شيء من الأشياء

words: يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَىٰهُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلْغُيُوبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb describes God's continually renewed knowledge of successive secrets and conversations, while the intensive nominal form describes enduring, abundant knowledge of innumerable unseen things, giving the sentence force and eloquence.
rows.anchor: بصيغة الفعل الدال على الحدوث والتجدد والعلم المتعلق بالغيوب الكثيرة بصيغة الاسم الدال على الدوام والمبالغة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that, after being released, the confessors came with their wealth and asked the Prophet to give charity from it and seek forgiveness for them; he replied that he had not been commanded to take anything, and the verse was revealed. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: أخرج غير واحد عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم لما أطلقوا انطلقوا فجاءوا بأموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narrations say the Prophet then took one third of their wealth.
rows.anchor: فأخذ صلى الله عليه وسلم منها الثلث كما جاء في بعض الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because obligatory zakat had already been prescribed, al-Alusi takes this charity as expiation for their sins, in keeping with its stated purifying effect.
rows.anchor: فليس المراد من الصدقة الصدقة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the charity is zakat; taking it here prevents people from thinking these men were like certain hypocrites whose charity was rejected.
rows.anchor: وعن الجبائي أن المراد بها الزكاة وأمر صلى الله عليه وسلم بأخذها هنا دفعا لتوهم إلحاقهم ببعض المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the expiation reading, 'their wealth' refers to these men who confessed; on the zakat reading, it may refer to owners of wealth generally.
rows.anchor: فضمير أموالهم لهؤلاء المعترفين وقيل : إنه على الثاني راجع لأرباب الأموال مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'wealth' indicates that the collection is taken from all categories of property.
rows.anchor: وجمع الأموال للإشارة إلى أن الأخذ من سائر أجناس المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase may attach to 'take' or be an omitted circumstantial modifier of 'charity.'
rows.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بخذ ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من ( صدقة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ta in 'you purify them' addresses the Prophet; the jussive reading makes the clause a result of the command, while the nominative reading allows a circumstantial clause, an adjective for charity with an implied 'by it,' or an independent sentence, as Abu al-Baqa says.
rows.anchor: والتاء في ( تطهرهم ) للخطاب وقريء بالجزم على أنه جواب الأمر والرفع على أن الجملة حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the adjective construction, the ta may instead be feminine third person referring to the charity, with no need to supply 'by it' because the following phrase indicates it.
rows.anchor: وجوز على إحتمال الوصفية أن تكون التاء للغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the form tutahhiruhum, from the causative verb athhara, meaning the same as tahhara, 'to purify.'
rows.anchor: وقريء تطهرهم من أطهره بمعنى طهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the yā retained, 'and you purify them' may predicate an omitted subject, serve as a circumstantial clause attached to the command or its response, or begin a new sentence.
rows.anchor: بإثبات الياء وهو خبر مبتدأ محذوف والجملة حال من الضمير في الأمر أو في جوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a new sentence, it means the Prophet increases their good deeds or wealth through the charity, or intensifies their purification; interpreting it as raising them from hypocrites' ranks to sincere believers' ranks would imply they were hypocrites, contrary to the sounder view, and is tied here to the jussive reading.
rows.anchor: أي وأنت تزكيهم بها أي تنمي بتلك الصدقة حسناتهم وأموالهم أو تبالغ في تطهيرهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The apparent argument in al-Kashshaf makes the ta address the Prophet only, because the text says 'by it'; saying the charity itself purifies them is distant from Quranic eloquence.
rows.anchor: وظاهر مافي الكشاف يدل على أن التاء هنا للخطاب لا غير لقوله سبحانه : ( بها )

rows.speaker: مسلمة بن محارب
rows.claim: Muslama ibn Muharib reads the verb without its yā: tazakkahum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مسلمة بن محارب ( تزكهم ) بدون الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means pray and seek forgiveness for them; the preposition 'upon' is used because the verb carries a sense of kindness, and the ordinary supplication sense is more apparent than funeral prayer despite a report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: أي ادع لهم واستغفر وعدى الفعل بعلى لما فيه من معنى العطف

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i recommends the imam say to the giver: May God reward you for what you gave, make it purification for you, and bless what remains with you.
rows.anchor: واستحب الشافعي في صفته أن يقول للمتصدق آجرك الله فيما أعطيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some require the imam's prayer for a donor; others require it for obligatory alms but recommend it for voluntary charity, or require it of the imam and recommend it of the poor recipient. Al-Alusi's preferred ruling is recommendation in every case.
rows.anchor: والحق الاستحباب مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan is tranquility or what the soul rests in; one reading treats the Prophet's prayer itself as tranquility by hyperbole, another compares resorting to his prayer with resorting to a home, and al-Alusi prefers the first. His supplication soothes their hearts and assures them God has accepted them.
rows.anchor: والسكن السكون وما تسكن النفس إليه من الأهل والوطن مثلا وعلى الأول جعل الصلاة نفس السكن

rows.speaker: غير واحد من السبعة
rows.claim: Several of the seven canonical readers use the plural 'your prayers' to match the multiple people being prayed for.
rows.anchor: وقرأ غير واحد من السبعة ( صلواتك ) بالجمع مراعاة لتعدد المدعو لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears their confession, repentance, and supplication, and knows their regret, sorrow, and sincerity; alternatively He hears the Prophet's prayer and knows what wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: بما في الضمائر من الندم والغم لما فرط وبالا وبالإخلاص في التوبة والدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing names either reinforce the rationale for the prayer or form a concluding confirmation of the preceding two verses and all they contain.
rows.anchor: والجملة حينئذ تذليل للتعليل مقرر لمضمونه وعلى الأول تذليل لما سبق من الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Hud deny he brought clear proof either from stubborn resistance or because they are so blind to truth and inattentive to the signs that they misjudge a miracle; the prophets in fact brought manifest signs and miracles.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوه لفرط عنادهم أو لشدة عماهم عن الحق وعدم نظرهم في الآيات

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says every prophet was given signs of the kind by which people believed; al-Alusi invokes it to explain that the signs were real even when this passage does not name them.
rows.anchor: ففي الخبر ما من نبي إلا وقد أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving their gods means abandoning worship of them, and they say they will not do so because of Hud's bare assertion, unsupported by proof; here 'an' marks causation and attaches to 'leaving.'
rows.anchor: فعن للتعليل كما قيل في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some careful grammarians attach the prepositional phrase to an omitted circumstantial 'departing from,' rather than directly to 'leaving.'
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى أنه متعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من الضمير المستتر فيه أي صادرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms for departing from and returning to water became metaphors for acting and conducting affairs; a cited line uses issuing and drawing water as a metaphor for sound judgment in managing matters.
rows.anchor: وقد شاع في كلامهم استعمال الصدر والورد كناية عن العمل والتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can omit the word for returning to water because departure entails it, as in the saying that someone acts only on another's judgment; the phrase then means they will not leave their gods while acting on Hud's word.
rows.anchor: وقد يكتفى بالصد في ذلك لإستلزامه للورد فيقولون : لا يصدر إلا عن رأيه

words: وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَارِكِىٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوْلِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that analysis, negation applies both to the restriction and the main clause: they will neither leave their gods nor act on Hud's saying.
rows.anchor: والنفي فيه راجع إلى القيد والمقيد جميعا لأنهم لا يتركون آلهتهم ولا يعملون بقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes 'departing' to mean turning away, as a restriction on the negation, so they deny leaving their gods while turning away from Hud's words; it also answers Hud's command not to turn away.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن صادرين بمعنى معرضين وهو قيد للنفي والمعنى انتفى تركنا عبادة آلهتنا معرضين ( عن قولك )

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some analyze the construction as semantic inclusion rather than an omitted complement; al-Zamakhshari's wording appears to support this, as al-Kashf explains.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعضهم إرادة ذلك من باب التضمين لا من باب تقدير المتعلق بقرينة ( عن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean either that they do not believe what Hud brought or that they believe nothing he says or does, which includes his message.
rows.anchor: أي بمصدقين فيما جئت به أو في كل ما تأتي وتذر ويندرج فيه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeat their refusal to believe with a nominal sentence, added bā, and a fronted subject for emphasis, signaling that no hope of their believing remains.
rows.anchor: ثم كرروا ما دل عليه الكلام السابق من عدم إيمانهم بالجملة الاسمية مع زيادة الباء
